document.title: Reviews read every changed file
document.summary: Reviews now read every changed file, and a new eval case scores the facts unread files hide. Skill cleanup moves Refresh and cuts about 1,100 words.
document.why: Review agents complained about a limit of eight files, and [the requester thinks it hurts review quality](source:s1).

sources.label: Claude Code session · Nov 7
sources.gist: Asks why the limit exists and for a case that catches misses.

lookFor: [The request](source:s1) asks for an eval case that catches misses from unread files. `Must` and `Must not` scores do not change the exit code, so `vitadeck-144` shows a miss on its case line and cannot fail CI.

commits.subject: Skill: check claims outside the diff with git grep; trim and move Refresh
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A claim about code outside the diff, such as "nothing uses this export", now rests on one git grep batch at head. The skill asked for those facts while `show` prints only the diff. On vitadeck-144, Opus 5.5 high used one batch, which backed a lookFor bullet and made it drop a claim it could not check.

Cleanup, 6,684 words to 5,595 in SKILL.md:
- Refresh moves to references/refresh.md, behind a pointer that names when to read it. Its 772 words went out on every first-run call. It uses the <cli> placeholder, because only SKILL.md gets its pin rewritten.
- Step 4 points at each field's section instead of restating it with fewer conditions.
- Cut the copy of validate's checks, restated rules, and sentences the output already shows.
- serve runs as a background process, because it never returns.
- The local-executable rule sits with the CLI pin, and the example file has a condition for reading it.

Measured on vitadeck-144 with the eval grader against the skill before this commit. Opus 5.5 high: must 5/6, same as with no cap before these edits. Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor, two trials: must 1 and 2 of 6 against 2 and 0, false bullets 4 of 243 against 2 of 242, and all 109 files read in both trials. Producer tokens stay in the same range, at 5.0M and 6.8M against 3.1M and 6.2M. Smoke passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Skill: read every changed file; close the gaps that let unread code pass
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Past six files the skill allowed eight fetches. That budget came from the digest-first rewrite and was never measured alone, and it stayed at eight while source verdicts, attentions, and file notes came to rest on fetches. On a 110-file PR, reviews described most files from the digest, and some of those notes were false.

Fetch every file now, except pure renames and copies, moves, generated files with no hand-written code, and repeats of a mirror. A rename with edits and logic under build/ no longer get a "safe to skip" summary unread.

Measured on vitadeck-144 with the eval grader. Opus 5.5 high: must 2/6 to 5/6. Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor, two trials: false bullets 14 of 242 to 2 of 242, files read 8 to 91 and 109 of 109. Muse must stays at 0 to 2 of 6, and its producer tokens rise about 2 to 4 times.

Also from a scan of 11 runs and a review of the skill:
- Sources go to files and print their size, because a silent 10 KB cut cost 16 calls and left one run with half a PR body. A failed or absent source is named to the user.
- Say that zsh does not split a variable into words (46 fetches lost), that focus and notes are arrays (4 validate failures), and that a file note key is a file (1 failure).
- Route each fact to a field that can hold it, and require the listed facts in the document.
- Drop the digest-only path to an attention or question.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Eval: add vitadeck-144, a case for misses from unread files
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The case holds facts that only reading a file reveals, on a 110-file feature PR, and the mistakes reviews made when they described files they did not read. No earlier case was a large feature PR, and no eval counts fetches.

The grader now keys each bullet verdict by number. It returned 125 verdicts for 119 bullets on this case, and the count mismatch threw away the whole rubric.

linkedIssueNumbers reads a list after a closing keyword, such as "Closes #109, #110, and #111". It used to take only the first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
